statements.text: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (vEDS) occurs in approximately 1 in 50,000 to 1 in 200,000 individuals.
vEDS is caused by pathogenic variants in the COL3A1 gene, which encodes type III procollagen, a major protein in vessel walls and hollow organs.
Defective type III collagen results in marked fragility of arteries and hollow organs, predisposing affected individuals to spontaneous aneurysms, dissections, and rupture.
vEDS is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern.

vEDS is characterized by arterial, intestinal, and uterine fragility; thin, translucent skin; easy bruising; characteristic facial appearance (thin vermilion of the lips, micrognathia, narrow nose, prominent eyes); and an aged appearance to the extremities, particularly the hands.
Vascular dissection or rupture, gastrointestinal perforation, or organ rupture are the presenting signs in most adults with vEDS.
Arterial rupture may be preceded by aneurysm, arteriovenous fistulae, or dissection but also may occur spontaneously.
Approximately 60% of individuals with vEDS diagnosed before age 18 years are identified because of a positive family history.
Neonates with vEDS may present with clubfoot, hip dislocation, limb deficiency, and/or amniotic bands.
Approximately half of children tested for vEDS in the absence of a positive family history present with a major complication at an average age of 11 years.
Four minor diagnostic features – distal joint hypermobility, easy bruising, thin skin, and clubfeet – are most often present in children with vEDS ascertained without a major complication.

In a systematic review of 231 patients with vEDS, aneurysms were present in 40%, often multiple; arterial rupture without an underlying aneurysm occurred in 33%; and carotidocavernous fistula was seen in 18%.
The median age of death in vEDS patients was 31 years in a systematic review of treatment outcomes.
vEDS is associated with spontaneous pneumothorax as a potential complication.
Many patients with vEDS experience chronic pain and fatigue, sleep disturbances, and mental health challenges.
A randomized, controlled trial showed that celiprolol, a beta1 antagonist with beta2 partial antagonist properties, was associated with a 3-fold decrease in major vascular events related to vEDS.

In a retrospective cohort study, vEDS patients on a long-term angiotensin II receptor blocker and/or beta-blocker had fewer vascular events than those not on cardiac medication who received the same lifestyle advice.
After open surgery for vascular complications in vEDS, mortality was 30%; after endovascular procedures, it was 24%; and overall mortality across treatment modalities was 39%.

In a cohort of connective tissue disease patients undergoing aortic intervention at a high-volume center, vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome represented 5% of diagnoses; endovascular repair was increasingly used in carefully selected high-risk scenarios.
Research is underway to investigate metabolic phenotyping in vEDS, including adipose tissue function, insulin resistance, and diabetes risk.
Studies are exploring whether heart coherence training can help manage stress, anxiety, and blood pressure in vEDS patients.
Research is investigating local anesthetic resistance in EDS patients, including vEDS, to determine the frequency and mechanisms of resistance.
Artificial intelligence-based facial recognition tools are being developed to improve screening for vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and distinguish it from other types of EDS.
Research is investigating ultrastructural skin analysis as a potential surrogate marker for arterial integrity and tissue vulnerability in vEDS.
Studies are exploring nanoparticle-based delivery systems and elastin-stabilizing compounds to prevent aortic aneurysm expansion and rupture in connective tissue disorders including vEDS.
Research is investigating platelet function abnormalities in EDS patients to understand the mechanistic relationship between impaired platelet function and bleeding risk.
RaDiCo-SED-VASC is a national cohort registry in France dedicated to vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, currently recruiting patients.

VASCERN has developed six European rare vascular disease registries since 2019, including registries relevant to vascular diseases, which share common data elements and allow pooling of patient data across Europe.
Annabelle's Challenge maintains a database of over 600 genetically confirmed vEDS patients and is committed to patient-centred research following the principle of 'Nothing About Us Without Us'.

The Registry of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (RED) is a retrospective and prospective registry in Italy designed for care and research purposes, collecting personal, clinical, genetic, genealogical, and surgical data.
A national network for cardiovascular genomics is being developed in Brazil to create a registry of patients with hereditary cardiovascular diseases, combining clinical and genomic data.
